narrative:
The assessment estimated your chance of bad credit at 33%, meaning about one in three applicants with a similar profile would be expected to have repayment difficulty. That is not a certainty, but it was above the bank’s acceptance cutoff, so the loan was denied.

The strongest influence on the decision was the presence of a guarantor, and it worked in your favour by lowering the assessed risk. The second most influential factor was your checking-account status: being below zero DM pushed the assessment toward bad credit and was the main adverse signal. Accounts in that state are much less common among approved applicants (12.6%) than accounts with no overdraft (59.2%). The third factor was the amount requested: at 1,755 DM, it is below the approved average of 3,019.64 DM, so it modestly reduced risk rather than increased it. Overall, the helpful factors were not enough to offset the negative checking-account signal and the other circumstances in your profile.

Next, ask the lender what threshold or conditions would make a future application acceptable. Focus on clearing the overdraft and keeping the account in good standing, and ask whether a smaller or shorter loan, or keeping the guarantor, would improve your position.
